newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-SPAIN TO MEET AUSTRALIA IN WORLD TEAM FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SPAIN TO MEET AUSTRALIA IN WORLD TEAM FINAL.

text.p: Felix Mantilla and Albert Costa ensured Spain will meet Australia in the final of the World Team Cup by overpowering the Netherlands on Saturday.
It will be Spain's fifth appearance in the final with two of their three titles gained at the expense of Australia who will have to produce something special to avoid another defeat.
The Spaniards have been almost untouchable on clay this season, filling 14 of the 28 semifinal spots in seven European clay court events this season and winning four titles.
In their three Blue Group ties in this event, Spain did not lose a match and dropped just two sets in clinching their final place.
Mantilla's and Costa's performances have confirmed them as two of several Spanish contenders for the French Open crown when play begins on Monday.
Costa made it through his three round-robin matches without losing set, pushing Spain into the final with a 6-1 7-6 win over Jan Siemerink.
After losing the first set of his opening match, Mantilla has also been in prime form, dropping just five games in his next two matches including a 6-1 6-1 dismantling of Paul Haarhuis.
The turning point of the match came in the fourth game of the first set which went to deuce 13 times before Mantilla finally broke Haarhuis to go up 3-1.
The effort seemed to take everything out of the Dutchman who only won one of the next 10 games.
In the other Blue Group tie, Germany beat Sweden.
Martin Sinner, playing his first singles match of the championships for Germany, downed Magnus Larsson 7-6 7-6 while Michael Stich fought back to beat Magnus Gustafsson 2-6 7-6 6-4.
Stich's performance however, was not enough to convince him to play in the French Open.
The 1991 Wimbledon champion confirmed after the match he would definately not be at Roland Garros.

A finalist at the French Open last year, Stich said on Thursday he would not play in Paris because of a nagging shoulder injury but next day said he was reconsidering his decision after talking to tournament officals.
"I had talked to the referee in Paris and he asked me to reconsider and give it one more try," said Stich. "I played decent today but my shoulder still hurts and my serve is not there.
"This was three sets and in Paris you have to serve well for four-or-five sets and I'm not capable of that."
